documents.taskPrompt: Some people think secondary school students learn more through group projects, while others believe individual assignments are more useful. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
documents.essay:
Schools use different ways to help teenagers learn, and group projects are becoming quite common. Some parents prefer students to finish work alone because they can see each child's ability. I think both methods are needed, but they should have different purposes.

Working in a group can make a difficult task less frightening. For example, when students prepare a presentation about their town, one can interview residents while another finds pictures. They have to explain their ideas with other members, which sometimes shows a mistake they did not notice before. Quiet students may also feel more comfortable speaking to three classmates than to a whole class. These are useful experiences beyond the information in a textbook.

However, a group result does not always show what everyone has learned. In my school experience, the student who was good at making slides often did most of the project. Other members only read a few sentences at the end. They received similar marks although their effort was very different. Individual homework gives students a chance to struggle with a question themselves. It also lets teachers discover who actually needs more explanation.

In my view, teachers could use group work for exploring a topic and then ask each student to write a short personal answer. This answer need not be another large assignment. It could simply explain one decision the group made and whether the student agrees with it. In this way, cooperation would not replace personal thinking. Schools should teach students to work with others, while still making sure that every student has something of their own to say.

documents.taskPrompt: All secondary school students should take a compulsory course about managing personal money. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Young people will need to make decisions about money after leaving school, but many have little experience with it. Therefore, some people want personal finance to become a compulsory school subject. I mostly agree, although it should be a short practical course rather than another major examination.

There are everyday problems that teenagers can understand already. They buy phone packages, pay for online games and sometimes borrow money from friends. A course could show them how small monthly payments add up over a year. For example, a cheap subscription may seem harmless until a student pays for five similar services. Learning to compare the total cost is more helpful than just hearing adults tell them to spend less.

Another reason is that families give very different advice. Some parents discuss bills openly, while others think money is not a child's business. As a result, a student may enter university without knowing how to plan a month's food costs. Schools can give everyone some basic knowledge. However, teachers should avoid presenting one lifestyle as the correct choice. Spending on a hobby is not automatically wrong if the person has considered other needs.

I do not support turning this subject into a heavy written exam. Students might remember definitions of interest but still fail to read a real bank notice. Instead, they could plan a simple budget and explain what they would change when an unexpected cost appears.

Overall, basic money education deserves a place in secondary school. Its success should depend on whether students can handle ordinary decisions, not whether they can use complicated financial words.

documents.taskPrompt: Many universities now provide recordings of all lectures for students to watch later. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this development?
documents.essay:
University students can now watch many of their lectures again on a computer. This was less common when my parents studied. Recordings are convenient and can support learning, although they may also encourage students to put their work off.

The biggest advantage is that students can learn at a suitable speed. During a live lecture, a teacher may explain an important point while a student is still writing the previous one. With a recording, the student can stop and listen again. This is especially useful for someone studying in a second language. Also, students who miss a class because of illness do not have to depend completely on a friend's incomplete notes.

On the other hand, having every lecture available can create a false feeling that there is plenty of time. A student may skip Monday's class, promise to watch it on Friday, and then find three more recordings waiting. Watching several hours together before an exam is tiring. It is also easy to keep a video playing while looking at messages, without understanding much of it.

Another limitation is that a recording cannot fully reproduce a classroom discussion. The questions from other students may be hard to hear, and the viewer cannot immediately ask their own question. Universities should therefore keep opportunities for students to meet teachers. A short discussion session would be useful even when most teaching material is online.

In conclusion, recorded lectures are a helpful backup and a way to review difficult sections. However, students still need a regular study routine. Access to a large collection of videos alone does not mean that they will spend enough attention on the subject.

documents.taskPrompt: In some secondary schools, students rarely read books for pleasure outside class. What are the main reasons for this, and what could schools do to encourage voluntary reading?
documents.essay:
Some teenagers only open a book when a teacher tells them to do so. This worries adults who remember enjoying stories when they were young. I believe the problem is partly about competing activities and partly about the way reading is presented at school.

First, phones offer entertainment with very little waiting. A short video can become interesting in a few seconds, while a novel may take several chapters. After a busy school day, students often choose the easier activity. Homework also matters. If pupils have already spent two hours answering exercises, another book can feel like extra work, even when it is supposed to be enjoyable.

Schools sometimes make this feeling worse. They give everyone the same reading list and require a detailed report for every book. This may help teachers check progress, but students can start reading only to find information for the report. Some even choose the shortest book so they can finish the task quickly. A student who dislikes a difficult classic may wrongly conclude that all reading is boring.

To improve the situation, libraries could offer more choice, including comics, sports biographies and short stories. Teachers could let pupils stop a book they truly dislike and try another one. Occasional conversations about interesting scenes may work better than a formal report every week. Schools should also leave a little quiet reading time during the day, so reading does not always compete with unfinished homework.

In conclusion, students need both time and a reason to read. Schools cannot make every teenager love books, but they can avoid making voluntary reading feel like another test.

documents.taskPrompt: Schools should spend more money on educational trips, even if this means spending less on classroom equipment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Educational trips are a happy memory for many students. Some people think schools should organise more of them and reduce spending on classroom equipment if necessary. I agree that trips are valuable, but I would not make this change in every school.

Going outside school can make lessons more interesting. A student may forget a page about old buildings but remember walking inside a castle. Seeing real objects gives a different feeling from looking at a picture. Trips also give classmates time to talk in a relaxed place. Students who do not usually speak to each other may become friends while sitting together on a bus.

However, classroom equipment is used much more often. A trip may last one day, while desks, computers and science tools are used throughout the year. If a school does not have enough working equipment, students could have difficulty with ordinary lessons. For example, science is more hard to understand when pupils can only watch the teacher doing every experiment. Buying basic tools would probably help more than visiting a famous museum once.

The right decision also depends on the destination. A nearby park can be useful for a biology lesson and may not cost much. An expensive journey to another city is not necessarily more educational. Teachers need to connect the visit with something students are learning, otherwise it might just become a day for taking photos and buying snacks.

Overall, I would like schools to provide some trips because students enjoy them and can learn something outside books. However, schools should first have the equipment needed for daily lessons, and then choose affordable places to visit.

documents.taskPrompt: Frequent use of navigation apps makes people less able to find their way independently. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Navigation apps are now part of many people's daily journeys. Some people worry that using them frequently makes us worse at finding our own way. I agree to a certain extent, although the problem depends on how people use the instructions.

An app normally gives one small action at a time, such as turning left at the next street. The user can follow these actions without knowing where the destination is in relation to the starting point. I have experienced this myself. After following my phone to a restaurant twice, I still could not describe the route to a friend. I remembered the voice telling me to turn, but not the names of the streets.

This habit can become a problem when the phone loses power or the road is closed. Someone who has noticed important buildings can choose another direction more easily. A person who only looks at the blue line may feel lost immediately. It is therefore useful to look at the whole route before starting and pay attention to the surroundings.

However, it would be unfair to say that apps only damage our ability. They can help people explore unfamiliar areas which they would otherwise avoid. A map can also show how different districts connect. Drivers have enough things to watch already, so spoken directions can reduce the need to read signs at a busy crossing.

In conclusion, navigation apps can weaken our sense of direction when we follow them without any thinking. They remain useful tools, especially in a new place. We should use their information while still trying to build a rough picture of the journey ourselves.

documents.taskPrompt: Some people believe video calls are enough to maintain close family relationships across long distances. Others think regular face-to-face visits are necessary. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
documents.essay:
Many families live in different cities or even different countries. Video calls allow them to see each other without travelling. Some people consider these calls enough to keep a close relationship, while others believe family members must meet in person regularly.

There are good reasons to value video calls. They can turn contact into an ordinary part of the week instead of a special event during holidays. A grandmother can see a child showing a new drawing, and parents can ask about a normal working day. These small conversations help relatives understand each other's lives. For families who cannot afford frequent flights, this contact may be the only realistic option.

Nevertheless, a call often shows only what someone chooses to put in front of the camera. A parent may say everything is fine even when they are struggling with cooking or cleaning. During a visit, relatives can notice these problems and provide practical help. They can also share activities without needing to keep a conversation going all the time. Eating together or taking a walk can feel more natural than sitting in front of a screen.

I think both kinds of contact matter, but there should not be a fixed rule about how often families must travel. Long journeys can be expensive and tiring. Some workers have very few days of leave. Making them feel guilty will not create a warmer relationship.

Overall, video calls are very useful for keeping family members involved in everyday life. Visits can add things that a screen cannot provide, especially shared time and practical care. Families should choose a mixture that fits their circumstances rather than judge closeness only by the number of visits.

documents.taskPrompt: An increasing number of household appliances can connect to the internet and be controlled by phone. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
documents.essay:
Household appliances are becoming more connected. People can start a washing machine or change the room temperature through an app, even when they are outside. Although this technology is attractive, I do not think connecting every appliance brings enough benefit for an ordinary household.

There are some useful situations. A person returning from work can turn on the heating shortly before arriving, instead of leaving it on all afternoon. A connected device may also send a warning when water is leaking. These functions solve clear problems and could prevent a large amount of waste or damage. For somebody with difficulty moving around, controlling appliances from one place can be especially helpful.

However, many extra functions are less necessary. Starting a washing machine by phone still requires someone to put clothes inside it first. If the normal buttons work well, downloading another app does not save much effort. Family members may even need separate accounts for several machines, which makes a simple household job more confusing.

There is also the question of how long these products remain usable. People often keep a fridge for many years, but a company may stop updating its app much earlier. It would be frustrating if a working machine lost important functions because of a software problem. Ordinary controls should therefore continue to work without an internet connection.

In conclusion, connected appliances can be worthwhile when they offer a specific service, such as a warning or help with movement. However, I would not choose a product just because it can be controlled on a phone. A reliable machine with clear buttons is still the better choice for many daily tasks.

documents.taskPrompt: False information is often shared widely on social media before it is corrected. Why does this happen, and what could be done to reduce it?
documents.essay:
False stories can travel quickly through social media, while the correction receives much less attention. This happens for several reasons. I believe both the design of the platforms and the habits of users need to change.

One reason is that surprising messages are interesting to share. A claim that a common food is suddenly dangerous may make people worried about their family. They forward it immediately because they want to help, not because they intend to tell a lie. However, a message from a friend can seem trustworthy even if that friend has no knowledge about the subject.

Another reason is the speed of online sharing. It takes only a moment to press a button, but checking the original source may take several minutes. Some posts do not even include a date, so an old event can look like it happened today. Once many accounts repeat the same story, readers may think that several independent sources have confirmed it.

Platforms could make the source and publication date easier to see. When someone shares a story without opening it, a short reminder to read it first may also be useful. However, removing every uncertain statement would be difficult, and sometimes new information is still developing. Users should be taught to look for the original report and compare it with another reliable source.

Corrections also need to reach the people who saw the first post. A separate announcement on a different page is unlikely to do this.

In conclusion, false information spreads through strong feelings and very easy sharing. Reducing it requires small pauses before forwarding, clearer sources and corrections that follow the original message.

documents.taskPrompt: People now take many more photographs during holidays than in the past. Why has this change happened? Do you think it helps people enjoy and remember their holidays?
documents.essay:
Taking photographs has become a normal part of almost every holiday. People photograph their food, hotels and even tickets. This change is mainly connected with smartphones, and I think it has both good and bad effects on the holiday experience.

In the past, people needed to carry a camera and sometimes pay to print their pictures. Now most travellers already have a phone in their pocket. They can take fifty photos without worrying about the cost. Social media gives them another reason to do it. When friends share beautiful travel pictures, people may want to show their own experiences as well.

Photographs can certainly help us remember a trip. A picture of a small restaurant might bring back the taste of a meal and a conversation with the owner. Photos are also useful for telling family members about places they have never visited. My parents enjoy seeing the pictures after a travel, especially when there are people in them rather than only buildings.

However, trying to get a perfect picture can take a surprising amount of time. Some visitors queue at one famous spot and leave immediately after taking their photo. They may remember the queue more clearly than the place itself. If friends disagree about taking pictures, this can also make the day less relaxed.

For me, it is better to take a few photos and then put the phone away for a while. There is no need to record every meal or street. Overall, cameras make holiday memories easier to keep, but enjoying the actual day should come first. A large photo collection is not always the sign of a good journey.

documents.taskPrompt: Restaurants should stop providing disposable cutlery with takeaway meals unless customers specifically request it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Takeaway meals often arrive with plastic forks, spoons and sometimes several packets of tissues. Many of these items are not used. I agree that restaurants should provide disposable cutlery only when a customer asks for it, although the choice should be easy to find.

The main reason is that many takeaway meals are eaten at home. People already have their own spoons and chopsticks there, so the new set may go straight into a drawer or a bin. I used to keep these small packets because throwing them away felt wasteful. After a few months, there were far more than I could use. This shows that giving something automatically does not mean it is needed.

Asking customers to choose would reduce this unnecessary material without changing the food itself. Ordering apps could remember a person's preference, while telephone orders could include a simple question. Restaurants would also purchase fewer items that customers never open. The saving from one meal is small, but a busy shop prepares many meals every day.

However, some people order lunch to an office or eat while travelling. They may not have any cutlery with them. If a restaurant removes everything without a clear notice, these customers could have trouble eating their meal. Staff should still be able to include a set when it is requested, and the option should not be hidden at the end of a long page.

In conclusion, disposable cutlery should be available when necessary rather than included in every bag. This is a fairly easy change because it asks customers what they need. It can reduce waste while keeping takeaway meals convenient.

documents.taskPrompt: A large amount of food bought by households is thrown away uneaten. What causes this problem, and what practical steps could reduce it?
documents.essay:
Many households throw away food although they spend a considerable part of their income buying it. People do not usually plan to waste food. In my opinion, the problem often begins with shopping habits and continues because they forget what is already at home.

Supermarkets encourage customers to buy large packs and special offers. A family may buy three bags of vegetables because each bag costs less, even when they only need one. The unused food then becomes soft before anyone cooks it. People also shop when they are hungry or without checking the fridge, which can result in buying the same things again.

Busy schedules create another difficulty. Someone may plan to cook every evening but later stay at work or eat with a friend. Fresh ingredients remain in the fridge while the original plan is forgotten. Simply telling people to be responsible does not solve this change in their daily routine.

A useful first step is to check existing food before making a short shopping list. It is also sensible to plan only a few meals ahead, rather than buy fresh food for an ideal week that may not happen. Food which needs eating soon could be placed together where everyone can see it. Freezing spare portions is another option, provided that people write the date and remember to use them.

Shops can help by selling smaller quantities without making them much more expensive. Customers should not have to buy more than they can finish to get a reasonable price.

Overall, reducing household food waste requires realistic planning. Buying a bargain is not really saving money if half of it finally goes into the bin.

documents.taskPrompt: Some people want city parks to have neatly cut grass and formal gardens. Others prefer parks with more natural areas for plants and wildlife. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
documents.essay:
City parks give residents a place to relax, but people do not all want the same appearance. Some prefer short grass and carefully arranged flowers, while others would like more areas to grow naturally. I think parks can include both, depending on how each part is used.

A tidy park is attractive and comfortable for many activities. Children need open ground for games, and families may want to sit on clean grass. Clear paths also help older visitors walk without worrying about uneven ground. When a park is very untidy, people may think nobody is looking after it and become less willing to visit.

On the other hand, cutting every area in the same way leaves fewer places for insects and birds. A corner with long grass or fallen leaves can provide shelter for small animals. It may also be more interesting for children than another empty lawn. They can watch changes through the seasons and see that nature is not always shaped like a garden in a picture.

The difficulty is making a natural area look intentional. If visitors only see tall weeds beside a broken bench, they may regard it as poor maintenance. Park managers could keep paths clear and put a small sign explaining why some areas are left to grow. There should still be regular checks for rubbish and dangerous branches.

In my view, the choice does not have to cover the whole park. Busy spaces near playgrounds can be kept tidy, while quieter corners can support wildlife. A successful park should provide places for people to use and some room for living things that do not need a perfectly cut lawn.

documents.taskPrompt: Documentaries about nature and environmental problems have become popular in many countries. Why do people watch these programmes? Do you think they encourage people to protect the environment?
documents.essay:
Nature documentaries attract many viewers today. They show places that most of us will never visit, such as deep oceans and cold mountains. I think people mainly watch them because they are beautiful and interesting, and they can also make viewers care more about environmental problems.

Modern cameras are one reason for their popularity. We can see small insects very closely or follow an animal moving through a forest. These pictures are exciting even for people who do not normally enjoy science. The programmes are often easy to watch with family members because they do not require much background knowledge. A clear story about one animal can hold a child's attention.

Another reason is that city life can become repetitive. People spend much of the day between home and work, surrounded by roads and buildings. Watching a programme about wild places gives them a short break from this routine. Some viewers may later become interested in visiting a park or learning more knowledge about a particular species.

These documentaries can encourage protection by showing what is being lost. It is easier to feel concerned about polluted water after seeing the animals which live there. However, concern does not always lead to action. After the programme ends, viewers might return to their normal habits. The problem can seem so large that their own actions feel unimportant.

I believe programmes should include a few clear things people can do, without making the whole film a lecture. Schools could also discuss them with students. Overall, nature documentaries are useful because they bring distant places into ordinary homes. They cannot solve environmental problems alone, but they may give people a starting interest.

documents.taskPrompt: Some natural attractions limit the number of visitors allowed each day. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this policy?
documents.essay:
Popular natural attractions can receive thousands of visitors on a single day. To prevent damage, some places only sell a limited number of tickets. This policy has clear benefits, but it can also cause difficulties for visitors and nearby businesses.

The main benefit is giving the place time and space to recover. When too many people walk beside a narrow path, plants can be damaged and the bare ground becomes wider. Noise and rubbish may also disturb wildlife. A daily limit makes it easier for staff to manage these problems. It can improve the visit as well, because people are able to enjoy the view without standing in a crowded line.

However, a fixed limit can be inconvenient. A family may travel a long distance and find that all tickets have been booked. Local cafes and small hotels may receive fewer customers, especially if they depend on a short holiday season. Some visitors might go to nearby unprotected places instead, moving the damage rather than reducing it.

For these reasons, managers should explain the booking rules clearly before people travel. They could also offer different entry times to spread visitors through the day. The limit should be based on the condition of the area, not just copied from another attraction. A wide beach and a small mountain path cannot hold the same number of people.

In conclusion, visitor limits can protect fragile places and make the experience more pleasant. Nevertheless, they work better with clear information and attention to the surrounding area. The purpose should be to keep a place worth visiting in the future, while helping today's visitors understand why some restrictions are necessary.

documents.taskPrompt: Some companies require new employees to spend short periods working in several departments before choosing a permanent role. Do the advantages of this approach outweigh the disadvantages?
documents.essay:
Some companies move new employees through different departments before giving them a permanent position. This can take several months. I think the advantages usually outweigh the disadvantages for people starting their first job, as long as the programme has a clear end.

A new worker may know the name of a job without understanding its daily activities. For example, someone who wants to work in sales may discover that they dislike making repeated phone calls. A short period in another department could help them find work that suits them better. It also gives the company more information than an interview can provide.

Working in several teams can help employees understand how their own decisions affect others. A person who has spent time dealing with customer complaints may write clearer product instructions later. They have seen the confusion directly, rather than only being told that clear writing is important. Knowing colleagues in other teams can also make it easier to ask for help.

However, moving too frequently has a cost. Each department needs to explain basic tasks again, and the employee may leave just when they become useful. Some workers could feel that they are always a beginner. They might also receive simple jobs in every department without getting a serious chance to learn.

Companies should therefore give each placement a clear task and enough time to finish it. New workers also need someone to discuss their experiences with. Otherwise, rotation may become little more than changing desks.

Overall, trying different roles can help new employees make a better choice and understand the company. It should lead towards a stable job, rather than keep them moving because managers have not decided where to put them.

documents.taskPrompt: Some employers find that young employees leave their jobs within the first year. What might cause this, and what could employers do to encourage them to stay?
documents.essay:
Employers sometimes spend time teaching young workers and then lose them within a year. It is easy to blame this on a lack of patience. However, I think the reasons are often more practical, and companies need to understand them before trying to keep staff.

One common problem is a gap between the advertised job and the real one. An interview may describe interesting projects, but the new employee mostly copies information into forms. Some routine work is unavoidable, especially at the beginning. Yet if nobody explains how this work connects to a later role, the person may feel that staying will change nothing.

Pay and working hours also matter. Young workers have rent and transport costs, even if they do not have children. A slightly better salary nearby can make a real difference. Frequent last minute requests to work late may also push them to leave, particularly when managers described the company as having a good balance between work and life.

Employers could start by giving a more honest picture during recruitment. A difficult part of the job is less disappointing when it was explained in advance. After the worker joins, regular short conversations can help managers notice problems early. These talks should lead to actual changes when possible, rather than simply ask the employee to be more positive.

Companies will not keep every young worker. Some people discover that they want a completely different career, and this is reasonable.

In conclusion, early departures can reflect poor expectations, limited development or unsatisfactory conditions. Employers are more likely to keep people by improving their daily experience than by giving speeches about loyalty to the company.

documents.taskPrompt: Some people say a high salary is the most important feature of a good job. Others think doing meaningful work matters more. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
documents.essay:
When choosing a job, people often compare money with the feeling that their work is useful. Some consider a high salary the main sign of a good job, while others put meaningful work first. I believe this choice depends partly on a person's situation, but money alone is not enough for a satisfying working life.

A good salary can remove a lot of everyday worry. Workers need to pay rent, support family members and prepare for unexpected costs. Someone who is worried about next month's bills may not have much freedom to choose a job because it is interesting. It would be unrealistic to tell this person that money does not matter. Higher pay can also give people more choices outside work.

On the other hand, work takes up a large part of most adults' lives. A person may earn well but feel unhappy if they believe their tasks have no purpose. Meaningful work does not have to be a famous profession such as medicine. A repair worker may feel proud when an old machine works again, and a shop assistant may enjoy helping regular customers.

There can also be a problem with expecting a job to provide all meaning in life. People can care about their families, hobbies or community activities. They should not feel ashamed of doing an ordinary job mainly for a stable income.

My view is that a job should first provide acceptable pay and conditions. After these needs are met, meaningful tasks become more important than every further increase in salary. The best choice is personal, and a good job should make life manageable as well as give some reason to keep doing it.

documents.taskPrompt: Employees should normally be expected to answer work messages outside their paid working hours. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Phones make it possible for employers to contact staff at almost any time. Some managers expect a quick answer even after the working day has finished. I disagree with making this a normal expectation, although certain jobs need an agreed arrangement for urgent situations.

The main problem is that a message can interrupt more than a few minutes. An employee eating with family may begin thinking about the next day's problem and stop paying attention to the people around them. Even when no message arrives, they may keep checking the phone because they are afraid of missing something. Their time at home then does not feel fully their own.

Answering messages at night can also hide problems in the organisation of work. If every task becomes urgent at the end of the day, perhaps the team has too many tasks or unclear deadlines. Expecting staff to stay available may make the problem less visible to managers, so there is little reason to improve the planning.

Of course, some situations are different. A broken system may need immediate attention, and international teams sometimes work in different time zones. The people responsible should know in advance when they must be available. They should also receive suitable pay or time off for this duty. It should not quietly become everyone's responsibility.

Employers can help by clearly marking messages that can wait until tomorrow and respecting that label themselves. Staff are unlikely to trust the rule if their manager complains about a slow evening reply.

Overall, being reachable all the time should not be part of an ordinary job by default. Clear working boundaries allow people to rest and make genuine emergencies easier to recognise.

documents.taskPrompt: Some employers provide games rooms, gyms and other leisure facilities inside the workplace. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this practice?
documents.essay:
Some companies now provide places where employees can exercise, play games or relax during the day. These facilities can make an office more attractive. However, I think their value depends on whether workers actually have the time and freedom to use them.

There are several possible benefits. Sitting at a desk for many hours can make people tired, so a short period of exercise may help them feel better. A games room can also allow workers from different teams to meet. They may have an easy conversation over a game when they would not normally speak in a meeting. This can make the workplace feel more friendly.

Facilities at work may also save employees a journey. Someone who wants to exercise after finishing their tasks does not need to travel to another gym. In a large city, this could be convenient. Employers may find it easier to attract applicants when the office looks comfortable and has something beyond desks and computers.

Nevertheless, these things cost money and take space. Some workers would prefer better chairs or a quieter place to concentrate. Others might have no interest in games. There is also a risk that the facilities look good in photographs but are rarely used because everyone is too busy. Employees may worry that their manager will think they are lazy if they take a break.

For these reasons, companies should ask staff what they would actually use and make breaks acceptable in practice. Overall, leisure facilities can be a pleasant addition to a workplace. They should not be treated as a replacement for reasonable workloads and a comfortable place to do the job.

documents.taskPrompt: Some people believe public libraries should mainly provide quiet places for reading. Others think libraries should also hold talks, clubs and community activities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
documents.essay:
Public libraries are often associated with silence, but many now organise different activities. Some visitors welcome this change, while others want a peaceful place to read. I believe both uses are valuable, provided that activities do not take away the quiet space people rely on.

A quiet library is important because not everyone has somewhere suitable to study at home. A student may share a bedroom with a brother, or a worker may live beside a noisy road. The library gives them a desk and a place where they can concentrate without buying anything. If every room is filled with conversation, this basic purpose becomes difficult to achieve.

However, libraries can also help people discover interests together. A book club might encourage someone to finish a novel they would otherwise give up. A talk by a local writer can bring attention to books that stay unnoticed on the shelves. Activities for children may make their first experience of the library enjoyable and encourage them to return.

The problem is often the arrangement of the building rather than the idea of activities itself. A lively children's session beside the main study tables will clearly disturb readers. A separate room or a limited time for events can reduce this difficulty. Libraries should tell visitors when noisy activities are planned so that they can choose when to come.

In my opinion, a library does not need to choose between being completely silent and becoming a general meeting hall. It can welcome conversation in some spaces while protecting quiet areas. Its activities should still have a clear connection with reading, learning or helping local people share knowledge.

documents.taskPrompt: Cities should provide some public transport late at night, even if these services carry fewer passengers than daytime services. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Many cities reduce or stop public transport late at night because fewer people use it. Some people think a limited service should still be provided. I agree, particularly on routes used by people finishing work, although running the whole daytime network would be unnecessary.

Not everybody travels according to office hours. Restaurant staff, cleaners and hospital workers may finish after the last normal bus. Without public transport, they might have to pay for a taxi or ask a family member to collect them. For a low paid worker, the cost can take a noticeable part of the day's earnings. A city benefits from these jobs continuing at night, so it should consider how the workers get home.

Late transport can also offer another choice to people going out with friends. Some may otherwise drive because they have no easy way back. A reliable bus on a main route could allow them to leave the car at home. It would not solve every problem linked with nightlife, but it could make the journey less complicated.

However, buses with almost no passengers still need drivers, fuel and maintenance. Cities should examine where late journeys actually happen. They could begin with a few routes near hospitals, busy workplaces and major residential areas. Clear departure times matter because waiting a long time at night is uncomfortable, especially in bad weather.

In conclusion, a smaller number of passengers is not by itself a good reason to remove every late service. The importance of the journey also matters. Cities should provide a modest night network based on real travel needs and check whether its routes and times are useful.

documents.taskPrompt: In many urban neighbourhoods, residents have little contact with the people living nearby. Why might this happen, and how could local communities encourage more contact?
documents.essay:
People in a city may live only a few metres apart but know almost nothing about each other. Some do not even recognise the person next door. This is partly caused by busy routines and frequent moving, and communities can help by creating simple chances to meet.

Many residents leave home early and return late. When they finally arrive, they want to rest rather than begin a conversation in the corridor. Apartment buildings can also make accidental contact less likely. People go directly from the lift into their own flat, and there may be no shared place where they naturally stay for a while.

Another reason is that neighbours often change. A tenant may only live in the building for six months. Residents who have seen many people come and go might stop making an effort to introduce themselves. Some people also worry about disturbing others, so they stay quiet even when they would like to have a more close relationship.

Local groups could organise small, regular activities rather than depend on one large yearly celebration. A weekend plant exchange or a short clean up of a shared garden gives people something to do together. Conversation can then begin around the activity, without requiring everyone to make a speech about themselves. A bench in a pleasant shared space may also help, if residents feel welcome to use it.

However, participation should remain optional. Some people value privacy, and good neighbours do not need to become close friends.

Overall, weak neighbourhood contact is often a result of daily habits rather than dislike. Repeated small meetings can make people more familiar, so asking for simple help later feels less awkward.

documents.taskPrompt: Local governments increasingly ask residents to complete tasks such as booking appointments and renewing permits online. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this change?
documents.essay:
Many local government services can now be used online. Residents can book an appointment or renew a permit without going to an office. This is convenient for many people, but difficulties appear when the online route becomes the only practical choice.

The main advantage is that people can complete simple tasks at a time that suits them. A worker does not need to take half a day off just to hand in a form. It is also easier to check the required documents before making a journey. When the website shows progress clearly, residents may avoid repeated phone calls asking whether their application has been received.

However, an online form cannot always answer an unusual question. A person's situation may not fit any of the choices on the screen. If there is no way to explain the problem, they can become stuck even though they understand how to use a computer. Technical confidence alone does not solve a badly designed process.

Some residents also lack a suitable device or need help reading instructions. Asking a relative to complete every official task can be uncomfortable because the information may be personal. A service which looks simple to its designers may therefore create a lot of difficulty for another person.

I think online services should cover the ordinary steps, while staff remain available for questions and unusual cases. Contact details should be easy to find, and residents should not have to restart the whole application when they ask for help.

Overall, moving services online can save journeys and make routine tasks easier. Its disadvantages are smaller when people can still reach someone who understands the problem behind the form.

documents.taskPrompt: Some city governments spend public money on free outdoor concerts and performances. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this spending?
documents.essay:
Free outdoor performances are a common feature of summer in some cities. Residents can listen to music or watch a show without buying a ticket. I think these events can improve city life, although they should be organised carefully and kept within a reasonable budget.

One advantage is that people can try something unfamiliar without planning a special evening. A family walking through a square may stop to watch a dance performance. Children might see an instrument they have never noticed before. If they do not enjoy the show, they can leave after a few minutes without feeling that they have wasted money.

Such events can also make a public place feel lively. People who normally hurry through the city have a reason to stay for a while. Local performers may get a chance to reach a larger audience than they would in a small private venue. Nearby shops could receive more customers, although this will depend on the location and the kind of event.

The disadvantages are mainly noise, rubbish and cost. Residents living beside the square may not want to hear music every weekend. Cleaning up after a large crowd also requires staff. An expensive concert could be difficult to justify if the city is struggling to repair basic facilities.

City governments should publish the event times and avoid running performances late into the night. A few smaller shows with local artists may be enough, rather than trying to invite famous singers.

In conclusion, free performances can give residents an enjoyable shared experience. They are a useful addition when the city can afford them, but their size and frequency should take account of the people who live nearby.

topicAssetPacks.sourceTitle: 合成考生 · 下班后回复工作消息
topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: Employees should normally be expected to answer work messages outside their paid working hours. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Phones make it possible for employers to contact staff at almost any time. Some managers expect a quick answer even after the working day has finished. I disagree with making this a normal expectation, although certain jobs need an agreed arrangement for urgent situations.

The main problem is that a message can interrupt more than a few minutes. An employee eating with family may begin thinking about the next day's problem and stop paying attention to the people around them. Even when no message arrives, they may keep checking the phone because they are afraid of missing something. Their time at home then does not feel fully their own.

Answering messages at night can also hide problems in the organisation of work. If every task becomes urgent at the end of the day, perhaps the team has too many tasks or unclear deadlines. Expecting staff to stay available may make the problem less visible to managers, so there is little reason to improve the planning.

Of course, some situations are different. A broken system may need immediate attention, and international teams sometimes work in different time zones. The people responsible should know in advance when they must be available. They should also receive suitable pay or time off for this duty. It should not quietly become everyone's responsibility.

Employers can help by clearly marking messages that can wait until tomorrow and respecting that label themselves. Staff are unlikely to trust the rule if their manager complains about a slow evening reply.

Overall, being reachable all the time should not be part of an ordinary job by default. Clear working boundaries allow people to rest and make genuine emergencies easier to recognise.

topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: Documentaries about nature and environmental problems have become popular in many countries. Why do people watch these programmes? Do you think they encourage people to protect the environment?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Nature documentaries attract many viewers today. They show places that most of us will never visit, such as deep oceans and cold mountains. I think people mainly watch them because they are beautiful and interesting, and they can also make viewers care more about environmental problems.

Modern cameras are one reason for their popularity. We can see small insects very closely or follow an animal moving through a forest. These pictures are exciting even for people who do not normally enjoy science. The programmes are often easy to watch with family members because they do not require much background knowledge. A clear story about one animal can hold a child's attention.

Another reason is that city life can become repetitive. People spend much of the day between home and work, surrounded by roads and buildings. Watching a programme about wild places gives them a short break from this routine. Some viewers may later become interested in visiting a park or learning more knowledge about a particular species.

These documentaries can encourage protection by showing what is being lost. It is easier to feel concerned about polluted water after seeing the animals which live there. However, concern does not always lead to action. After the programme ends, viewers might return to their normal habits. The problem can seem so large that their own actions feel unimportant.

I believe programmes should include a few clear things people can do, without making the whole film a lecture. Schools could also discuss them with students. Overall, nature documentaries are useful because they bring distant places into ordinary homes. They cannot solve environmental problems alone, but they may give people a starting interest.

topicAssetPacks.sourceTitle: 合成考生 · 城市公园应该整齐还是自然
topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: Some people want city parks to have neatly cut grass and formal gardens. Others prefer parks with more natural areas for plants and wildlife. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
City parks give residents a place to relax, but people do not all want the same appearance. Some prefer short grass and carefully arranged flowers, while others would like more areas to grow naturally. I think parks can include both, depending on how each part is used.

A tidy park is attractive and comfortable for many activities. Children need open ground for games, and families may want to sit on clean grass. Clear paths also help older visitors walk without worrying about uneven ground. When a park is very untidy, people may think nobody is looking after it and become less willing to visit.

On the other hand, cutting every area in the same way leaves fewer places for insects and birds. A corner with long grass or fallen leaves can provide shelter for small animals. It may also be more interesting for children than another empty lawn. They can watch changes through the seasons and see that nature is not always shaped like a garden in a picture.

The difficulty is making a natural area look intentional. If visitors only see tall weeds beside a broken bench, they may regard it as poor maintenance. Park managers could keep paths clear and put a small sign explaining why some areas are left to grow. There should still be regular checks for rubbish and dangerous branches.

In my view, the choice does not have to cover the whole park. Busy spaces near playgrounds can be kept tidy, while quieter corners can support wildlife. A successful park should provide places for people to use and some room for living things that do not need a perfectly cut lawn.

topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: People now take many more photographs during holidays than in the past. Why has this change happened? Do you think it helps people enjoy and remember their holidays?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Taking photographs has become a normal part of almost every holiday. People photograph their food, hotels and even tickets. This change is mainly connected with smartphones, and I think it has both good and bad effects on the holiday experience.

In the past, people needed to carry a camera and sometimes pay to print their pictures. Now most travellers already have a phone in their pocket. They can take fifty photos without worrying about the cost. Social media gives them another reason to do it. When friends share beautiful travel pictures, people may want to show their own experiences as well.

Photographs can certainly help us remember a trip. A picture of a small restaurant might bring back the taste of a meal and a conversation with the owner. Photos are also useful for telling family members about places they have never visited. My parents enjoy seeing the pictures after a travel, especially when there are people in them rather than only buildings.

However, trying to get a perfect picture can take a surprising amount of time. Some visitors queue at one famous spot and leave immediately after taking their photo. They may remember the queue more clearly than the place itself. If friends disagree about taking pictures, this can also make the day less relaxed.

For me, it is better to take a few photos and then put the phone away for a while. There is no need to record every meal or street. Overall, cameras make holiday memories easier to keep, but enjoying the actual day should come first. A large photo collection is not always the sign of a good journey.

topicAssetPacks.sourceTitle: 合成考生 · 社交平台上不实消息的传播
topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: False information is often shared widely on social media before it is corrected. Why does this happen, and what could be done to reduce it?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
False stories can travel quickly through social media, while the correction receives much less attention. This happens for several reasons. I believe both the design of the platforms and the habits of users need to change.

One reason is that surprising messages are interesting to share. A claim that a common food is suddenly dangerous may make people worried about their family. They forward it immediately because they want to help, not because they intend to tell a lie. However, a message from a friend can seem trustworthy even if that friend has no knowledge about the subject.

Another reason is the speed of online sharing. It takes only a moment to press a button, but checking the original source may take several minutes. Some posts do not even include a date, so an old event can look like it happened today. Once many accounts repeat the same story, readers may think that several independent sources have confirmed it.

Platforms could make the source and publication date easier to see. When someone shares a story without opening it, a short reminder to read it first may also be useful. However, removing every uncertain statement would be difficult, and sometimes new information is still developing. Users should be taught to look for the original report and compare it with another reliable source.

Corrections also need to reach the people who saw the first post. A separate announcement on a different page is unlikely to do this.

In conclusion, false information spreads through strong feelings and very easy sharing. Reducing it requires small pauses before forwarding, clearer sources and corrections that follow the original message.

topicAssetPacks.sourceTitle: 合成考生 · 家电联网是否值得
topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: An increasing number of household appliances can connect to the internet and be controlled by phone. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Household appliances are becoming more connected. People can start a washing machine or change the room temperature through an app, even when they are outside. Although this technology is attractive, I do not think connecting every appliance brings enough benefit for an ordinary household.

There are some useful situations. A person returning from work can turn on the heating shortly before arriving, instead of leaving it on all afternoon. A connected device may also send a warning when water is leaking. These functions solve clear problems and could prevent a large amount of waste or damage. For somebody with difficulty moving around, controlling appliances from one place can be especially helpful.

However, many extra functions are less necessary. Starting a washing machine by phone still requires someone to put clothes inside it first. If the normal buttons work well, downloading another app does not save much effort. Family members may even need separate accounts for several machines, which makes a simple household job more confusing.

There is also the question of how long these products remain usable. People often keep a fridge for many years, but a company may stop updating its app much earlier. It would be frustrating if a working machine lost important functions because of a software problem. Ordinary controls should therefore continue to work without an internet connection.

In conclusion, connected appliances can be worthwhile when they offer a specific service, such as a warning or help with movement. However, I would not choose a product just because it can be controlled on a phone. A reliable machine with clear buttons is still the better choice for many daily tasks.

topicAssetPacks.sourceTitle: 合成考生 · 视频通话能否替代家人见面
topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: Some people believe video calls are enough to maintain close family relationships across long distances. Others think regular face-to-face visits are necessary. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Many families live in different cities or even different countries. Video calls allow them to see each other without travelling. Some people consider these calls enough to keep a close relationship, while others believe family members must meet in person regularly.

There are good reasons to value video calls. They can turn contact into an ordinary part of the week instead of a special event during holidays. A grandmother can see a child showing a new drawing, and parents can ask about a normal working day. These small conversations help relatives understand each other's lives. For families who cannot afford frequent flights, this contact may be the only realistic option.

Nevertheless, a call often shows only what someone chooses to put in front of the camera. A parent may say everything is fine even when they are struggling with cooking or cleaning. During a visit, relatives can notice these problems and provide practical help. They can also share activities without needing to keep a conversation going all the time. Eating together or taking a walk can feel more natural than sitting in front of a screen.

I think both kinds of contact matter, but there should not be a fixed rule about how often families must travel. Long journeys can be expensive and tiring. Some workers have very few days of leave. Making them feel guilty will not create a warmer relationship.

Overall, video calls are very useful for keeping family members involved in everyday life. Visits can add things that a screen cannot provide, especially shared time and practical care. Families should choose a mixture that fits their circumstances rather than judge closeness only by the number of visits.

topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: Frequent use of navigation apps makes people less able to find their way independently. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Navigation apps are now part of many people's daily journeys. Some people worry that using them frequently makes us worse at finding our own way. I agree to a certain extent, although the problem depends on how people use the instructions.

An app normally gives one small action at a time, such as turning left at the next street. The user can follow these actions without knowing where the destination is in relation to the starting point. I have experienced this myself. After following my phone to a restaurant twice, I still could not describe the route to a friend. I remembered the voice telling me to turn, but not the names of the streets.

This habit can become a problem when the phone loses power or the road is closed. Someone who has noticed important buildings can choose another direction more easily. A person who only looks at the blue line may feel lost immediately. It is therefore useful to look at the whole route before starting and pay attention to the surroundings.

However, it would be unfair to say that apps only damage our ability. They can help people explore unfamiliar areas which they would otherwise avoid. A map can also show how different districts connect. Drivers have enough things to watch already, so spoken directions can reduce the need to read signs at a busy crossing.

In conclusion, navigation apps can weaken our sense of direction when we follow them without any thinking. They remain useful tools, especially in a new place. We should use their information while still trying to build a rough picture of the journey ourselves.

topicAssetPacks.sourceTitle: 合成考生 · 学校是否需要更多旅行
topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: Schools should spend more money on educational trips, even if this means spending less on classroom equipment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Educational trips are a happy memory for many students. Some people think schools should organise more of them and reduce spending on classroom equipment if necessary. I agree that trips are valuable, but I would not make this change in every school.

Going outside school can make lessons more interesting. A student may forget a page about old buildings but remember walking inside a castle. Seeing real objects gives a different feeling from looking at a picture. Trips also give classmates time to talk in a relaxed place. Students who do not usually speak to each other may become friends while sitting together on a bus.

However, classroom equipment is used much more often. A trip may last one day, while desks, computers and science tools are used throughout the year. If a school does not have enough working equipment, students could have difficulty with ordinary lessons. For example, science is more hard to understand when pupils can only watch the teacher doing every experiment. Buying basic tools would probably help more than visiting a famous museum once.

The right decision also depends on the destination. A nearby park can be useful for a biology lesson and may not cost much. An expensive journey to another city is not necessarily more educational. Teachers need to connect the visit with something students are learning, otherwise it might just become a day for taking photos and buying snacks.

Overall, I would like schools to provide some trips because students enjoy them and can learn something outside books. However, schools should first have the equipment needed for daily lessons, and then choose affordable places to visit.

topicAssetPacks.sourceTitle: 合成考生 · 学生为什么不愿课外阅读
topicAssetPacks.sourcePrompt: In some secondary schools, students rarely read books for pleasure outside class. What are the main reasons for this, and what could schools do to encourage voluntary reading?
topicAssetPacks.sourceEssaySnapshot:
Some teenagers only open a book when a teacher tells them to do so. This worries adults who remember enjoying stories when they were young. I believe the problem is partly about competing activities and partly about the way reading is presented at school.

First, phones offer entertainment with very little waiting. A short video can become interesting in a few seconds, while a novel may take several chapters. After a busy school day, students often choose the easier activity. Homework also matters. If pupils have already spent two hours answering exercises, another book can feel like extra work, even when it is supposed to be enjoyable.

Schools sometimes make this feeling worse. They give everyone the same reading list and require a detailed report for every book. This may help teachers check progress, but students can start reading only to find information for the report. Some even choose the shortest book so they can finish the task quickly. A student who dislikes a difficult classic may wrongly conclude that all reading is boring.

To improve the situation, libraries could offer more choice, including comics, sports biographies and short stories. Teachers could let pupils stop a book they truly dislike and try another one. Occasional conversations about interesting scenes may work better than a formal report every week. Schools should also leave a little quiet reading time during the day, so reading does not always compete with unfinished homework.

In conclusion, students need both time and a reason to read. Schools cannot make every teenager love books, but they can avoid making voluntary reading feel like another test.
